publication.title: iPhone OS Research Atlas
publication.scope: iPhone OS 1.1.4 / 4A102 and 3.1.3 / 7E18; native PinePhone execution, distinct QEMU gates and offline next-target study
publication.provenance: Original editorial synthesis of private project notebooks and experiment reports, with reviewed capture images, selected source excerpts and their provenance. Firmware, storage images, complete run artifacts and the implementation repository are not included.
publication.author: Felipe Sabino

record.title: Physical button edges reach original HID
record.method: Physical taps, visible response and post-run filesystem checks; separate QEMU poller control
record.observation: Three short physical power taps yielded setup image, black, setup image. In a separate boot each volume key delivered one Home/menu press-release pair. Both boots ended with clean recovery, fsck exit 0 and unchanged root.
record.limits: Touch, long power holds, volume auto-repeat and a complete home-screen interaction were not validated. The volume keys are mapped to Home, not audio volume.

excerpts.content:
The event callback calls the inherited
`dispatchKeyboardEvent` with Consumer page `0x0c`: usage `0x30` for Power
(the iPod hold/sleep-wake button) and usage `0x40` for either Volume key
(the iPod menu/Home button). These usages and the user-client path were
checked against the original 4A102 binary and SpringBoard's HID filter.

[…]

The LRADC at `0x01c21800` is polled with its IRQ disabled.
The live Jumpdrive tree declares Volume Up at 200 mV and Down at 400 mV on
channel 0, supplied by the 3 V ALDO3 rail. The A64's two-thirds reference
gives expected six-bit codes near 6 and 13, with bounded ranges on either
side of their midpoint.
excerpts.note: Exact selected notebook passages. Ellipses mark omitted material; source line numbers refer to the reviewed document.
